body: Files in `scene/` should not include editor-only code, even behind `#ifdef TOOLS_ENABLED`. You need to find a different way to expose this (perhaps in a way that projects can use, so this can also address https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10625).
This should not be defined repeatedly in _make_window() and set_visible().

Using the existing "project_metadata.cfg" and its `set_project_metadata` `get_project_metadata` may reduce the introduction of redundant code and "window_state.cfg".

Maybe can do `popup()` or `popup_centered_clamped()` here based on `Rect2 saved_size`
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/13ad17ea9bed98ffe9b1175fdb920eb0cb7daf0c/editor/gui/editor_quick_open_dialog.cpp#L187

Please use [Oxford comma](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/documentation/guidelines/docs_writing_guidelines.html#use-the-oxford-comma-to-enumerate-anything).

`_save_window();` can be replaced with `set_project_metadata` under `case NOTIFICATION_VISIBILITY_CHANGED` of `EditorQuickOpenDialog::_notification`, which will be triggered "when the window pops up" or "when the window is closed"

I was unable to use `set_project_metadata/get_project_metadata` or `NOTIFICATION_VISIBILITY_CHANGED` because this API is meant to be usable by game developers as well as us. 

`NOTIFICATION_VISIBILITY_CHANGED` on `EditorQuickOpenDialog` would defeat the purpose of the PR as that is specific to the `EditorQuickOpenDialog` node while this PR needs to work for any window that has a `session_id`.

`*_project_metadata` is only available in the editor but I did implement an equivalent version in `DisplayServer` to reduce repetition, if that is what you were getting at. I decided to not reuse `project_metadata.cfg` because I thought there might be section conflicts but if `EditorSettings` is the sole owner there may be conflicts about it's state.

The note about `popup` is interesting and I should address that soon, but I will need to figure out how `popup` is used/works first.
Can't this part be extracted into `_should_restore_window` (or rename to `_try_restore_window` ?) as the same code in set_visible?

There are a lot of processing about **popup rect** in those popup_* methods, may cause potential conflicts if place in `set_visible` or `_make_window`.

And these `popup_*` methods all contain Rect2i parameter. Logically speaking, this parameter should be used instead of bypassed. This will cause confusion for others in the future as to why the parameters passed in are useless.
